rules.description: Complete strong masculine singular/plural: uninflected nominative/accusative singular; -es, -e; plural -as, -a, -um, -as.
Complete strong heavy-stem neuter singular/plural: nominative/accusative singular and plural without ending; -es, -e; plural genitive -a and dative -um. Compounds follow the final nominal component.

Long/heavy feminine model ār: nominative singular uninflected; genitive/dative/accusative -e; plural nominative/accusative/genitive -a, dative -um. The alternate genitive plural -ena is not the selected route.
Feminine -nes doubles s before inflectional endings; the full singular/plural follows the long feminine model.
Weak masculine: nominative singular -a; other singular and nominative/accusative plural -an; genitive plural -ena; dative plural -um.

Weak neuter ēage has nominative/accusative singular ēage; genitive/dative singular ēagan; nominative/accusative plural ēagan; genitive plural ēagena (also ēagna); dative plural ēagum. Cook §53.2 explicitly gives neuter equality of nominative and accusative.

Wuldor uses the syncopated stem wuldr- before endings, by §§43.4 and 47.6. The selected reference nominative/accusative plural wuldru applies the admitted disyllabic neuter -u route (§47.1); it is a rule-derived reference cell, not a claim of corpus attestation or a new lexical plural meaning.
